title: The Myth of School Choice in Illinois
text:
In the recently passed Federal “Big Beautiful Bill,” an option for a school choice scholarship tax credit was passed in Congress and signed by President Trump. The official title is the Educational Choice for Children Act (ECCA). This tax credit provides Federal tax credit for taxpayers that donate to a 3rd party Scholarship Granting Organization (SGO).
When an SGO receives funds, the SGO will then pass those funds to students for use in attending alternative forms of schooling, such as private, micro, or homeschooling. Funds can be used for tutoring, books, online materials, educational therapies, and special needs services. The ECCA is totally separate from any state program. The US Department of Education and the IRS will administer and oversee the program.
But here is the rub. Each state must “opt-in” by the fall of 2026. Those states that do not voluntarily elect to participate will not be able to tap into the funds. This could mean students that really need a choice in their education will not have this benefit to improve their education.
Groups such as the Chicago Teachers Union (CTU) and their parents, the National Education Association (NEA) and American Federation of Teachers (AFT), do not like this at all. They say it will take funds away from public schools. False! No funds provided by the ECCA have any effect on reducing funds to government (public) schools. Let me repeat that—the ECCA has no effect at all on Federal, state or local funds going to government schools.
One of the arguments against school choice and the ECCA by the teacher unions is it will only benefit the “rich and wealthy” who already send their kids to private schools. I find that ludicrous since the wealthy already can afford to send their kids to private schools and do not need education scholarships for their kids.
Who really needs ECCA and school choice? Minority, disadvantaged students that are trapped in government schools with very poor outcomes. So why would teacher unions be so against an opportunity to improve the children they claim to be so concerned about? Could it be the children do not pay union dues and contribute to the political ideology the teacher unions advance?
Governor Pritzker has already stated he will be looking at ECCA. However, he already believes, at the behest of the teacher unions, that the ECCA will only benefit private schools and religious schools. He seems to ignore what will be best for students and their outcomes.
The Speaker of the Illinois House, Emanuel “Chris” Welch, stated school choice is a “tough issue in the state legislature.” If he can get 60 Democrats to support it, he “may” call the bill for a vote.
Let’s remember the $915 million in political contributions the four top government unions contributed in the last election cycle. I’m sure those political donations have nothing to do with making the school choice “tough issue” or Speaker Welch.
We will have to wait and see what Illinois does, but I wouldn’t hold your breath. CTU and other government unions are powerful and will definitely be calling the shots on this one.
Meanwhile, minority, disadvantaged students will continue to be on the sidelines with underperforming schools and sub-par education.
Isn’t politics grand?
